title: AEGIS: Adversarial Target-Guided Retention-Data-Free Robust Concept Erasure from Diffusion Models
claim: Models fine-tuned by existing erasure methods suppress target concepts for ordinary prompts but regain harmful content under adversarial prompts.
layout: 4 panels, left-to-right, pentagon radar charts with shared legend at right
description: Four pentagonal radar charts sit in a row with a shared legend at the far right. Each chart has five axes: Nudity, Impure, Erotic, Sexual and Naked. Five colored lines mark the prompt categories: blue for Nudity, orange for Naked, green for Sexual, red for Erotic and pink for Impure. Panel (a), d0 Original, shows small, compact polygons, so little harmful content appears. Panel (b), d1 ESD, shows large polygons that stretch toward the outer axes, with radial ticks at 10, 20 and 30. Panel (c), d2 ESD, shows small polygons again. Panel (d), d2 AET, shows large polygons again, similar to panel (b). The eye goes first to the contrast between the small polygons in (a) and (c) and the large ones in (b) and (d). Captions under each panel give the dataset and the erasure method.
caption: Adversarial prompts can still result in DMs fine-tuned by concept erasure methods generating images with harmful information.
abstract: Concept erasure helps stop diffusion models (DMs) from generating harmful content; but current methods face robustness retention trade off. Robustness means the model fine-tuned by concept erasure methods resists reactivation of erased concepts, even under semantically related prompts. Retention means unrelated concepts are preserved so the model's overall utility stays intact. Both are critical for concept erasure in practice, yet addressing them simultaneously is challenging, as existing works typically improve one factor while sacrificing the other. Prior work typically strengthens one while degrading the other, e.g., mapping a single erased prompt to a fixed safe target leaves class level remnants exploitable by prompt attacks, whereas retention-oriented schemes underperform against adaptive adversaries. This paper introduces Adversarial Erasure with Gradient Informed Synergy (AEGIS), a retention-data-free framework that advances both robustness and retention.
